Differentiate between nastic movements and tropic movements in plants.
options: Tropic movements are directional growth movements determined by stimulus direction (e.g. phototropism). Nastic movements
explanation: Tropic movements are directional growth movements determined by stimulus direction (e.g. phototropism). Nastic movements are non-directional growth/turgor responses independent of stimulus direction (e.g. folding of Touch-Me-Not leaves).

question: Draw a labeled diagram of human brain and describe functions of Forebrain, Midbrain, and Hindbrain.
options: Forebrain (Cerebrum): Main thinking part, voluntary actions, sensory interpretation, memory, hunger. Midbrain: Controls
explanation: Forebrain (Cerebrum): Main thinking part, voluntary actions, sensory interpretation, memory, hunger. Midbrain: Controls involuntary reflexes of head, neck, eyes. Hindbrain: Cerebellum controls posture, balance, precision of voluntary actions; Medulla controls blood pressure, salivation, vomiting; Pons regulates respiration.
